newsitem.title: USA: California official plans tobacco suits.
newsitem.headline: California official plans tobacco suits.

text.p: A judge on Friday cleared the way for California's Lieutenant Governor Gray Davis to sue tobacco companies to recover hundreds of millions of dollars of "illicit" profits by cigarette makers, Davis said.

California Superior Court Judge Robert May in San Diego rejected a motion by the tobacco industry to dismiss the lawsuit, which was filed in January by Davis acting as a private citizen on behalf of the state.
"It's a major victory for California taxpayers, and a blow to big tobacco," Davis, a Democrat, said at a news conference in San Francisco.
Judge May said Davis could proceed to trial to try to recover profits made by tobacco companies through allegedly fraudulent advertising about the dangers of smoking.

The judge struck down claims by Davis for repayment of costs associated with smoking-related illnesses, saying the state of California, not Davis, was the proper party to pursue the healthcare claims.
Davis said he filed the lawsuit because California Attorney General Dan Lungren, a likely rival in the 1998 campaign for governor, would not take action.
Lungren, a Republican, says that a California law bars him from joining other states in suing major tobacco companies.
State lawmakers are considering a bill to eliminate the special immunity from product liability lawsuits enjoyed by tobacco products in the state.
